breaking.change: A screen is on the stack once: pushing a screen that is already on the stack is refused with an error, where it stacked a second copy.
breaking.fix: Pop the screen before pushing it again, or use og.ui.replace.

breaking.change: A list a pushed screen iterates with {#each} has rows that each carry the key the each names ((row.id): a unique nonempty string id). A screen iterating any other list reports "each over '$rows' needs a keyed list; give each of its rows a unique string id" and is not drawn. A list the screen only reads whole is unaffected.
breaking.fix: Give each row of an iterated list a unique string in the field the each keys it by.

breaking.change: A pushed screen whose component instance leaves out a prop the component declares with no default is refused with "<file>:<line>: <Component> leaves out its prop '<name>'; pass it, or give it a default in the component", as a mounted document already was; the push used to build it with the prop unset.
breaking.fix: Pass every prop the component declares without a default (the built-in components declare none, so a built-in instance passes all its props, as the built-in screens do), or give your own component's prop a default with data-default on its <meta name="prop:…">.

breaking.change: A document whose root is a block ({#if}, {#each}) is refused with "a document's root is one element; put the block inside it".
breaking.fix: Wrap the block in one root element.

added.summary: og.ui.screenVm(screen) returns the screen's values as they are now: what was pushed, with what the screen's controls wrote through bind:, and each value the screen reads that the push left out (its prop's default, else null, or [] where the screen iterates it). It is null once the screen has left the stack.

fixed.summary: A pushed screen is built the way a mounted document is, so it resolves only the elements whose values changed and keeps its elements' state across frames. A dropdown or tooltip a layer opens is ordered just above that layer.
